sections.heading: Overview
bullets: Priya Raman and Mei Tanaka discussed platform workload, candidate Q4 bets, two backend hires, Mei’s growth toward a director role, and how product and engineering plan together.

sections.heading: Key points
bullets: Mei said three platform engineers had handled eleven after-hours pages in two weeks, alongside about twenty-six estimated hours of unplanned work.
Priya described mobile v2, an ETA accuracy model, and a staged self-serve onboarding pilot as proposals for the next day’s Q4 planning, not approved commitments.
Mei estimated ten usable engineering weeks after holidays and support work, with four weeks for mobile, three for ETA, and two reserved for reliability.
Mei said a new senior backend engineer would need about thirty days to learn the architecture and incident history before adding net capacity.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Priya backed a protected recovery afternoon after on-call duty, and Mei agreed to route urgent reviews to herself.
Priya and Mei agreed that the onboarding proposal should specify one carrier configuration, an import template, human review before activation, and a fallback that delays customer activation.
Priya agreed to invite Mei into a forty-five-minute scoping session before circulating the next cycle’s candidate bets.

sections.heading: Open questions
bullets: The Q4 planning group had not yet chosen its bets, approved the two backend hires, or decided whether to activate the onboarding pilot.
Mei and Priya still needed evidence that a pilot could shorten the nineteen-day onboarding process without increasing support tickets.

sections.heading: Pain points
bullets: Priya said new customers take an average of nineteen days to reach a first usable dispatch, creating pressure to improve onboarding.
Mei warned that a broken carrier import could damage customer trust more than a staged pilot would.

sections.heading: Current solution
bullets: Mei proposed testing one carrier configuration with an import template and human review before activation, while preserving a fallback to an import prototype without customer activation.

sections.heading: Objections
bullets: Mei objected to describing a broad self-serve launch for Q4 because platform reliability, mobile delivery, and ETA deployment already consume almost all estimated capacity.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Priya will present the three Q4 bets as proposals and include the gated pilot option in the next day’s planning draft.
Mei will send a capacity note by Friday so the planning group can evaluate the scope against pages and unplanned work.

sections.heading: Today
bullets: Mei Tanaka will tell the team today that the optional platform migration review is postponed to protect recovery time.
Priya Raman will revise the Q4 draft tonight and send it to Mei Tanaka tomorrow morning for a final read.

sections.heading: Blockers
bullets: Mei Tanaka said three platform engineers had handled eleven after-hours pages in two weeks and lacked a protected handoff after on-call duty.
Mei Tanaka said platform deployment, monitoring, and rollback work must be included in the three-week ETA estimate, while the two proposed hires cannot immediately relieve the Q4 load.

sections.heading: Goals
bullets: Priya Raman proposed evaluating mobile v2, ETA accuracy, and a staged self-serve onboarding pilot at the next day’s Q4 planning meeting.
Mei Tanaka wants to grow toward a director role by facilitating cross-team capacity decisions and delegating a service review.

sections.heading: Progress
bullets: Mei Tanaka estimated ten usable engineering weeks after holidays and existing support work, with four for mobile, three for ETA, and two reserved for reliability.
Priya Raman and Mei Tanaka defined a possible one-carrier onboarding pilot with an import template and human review.

sections.heading: Risks
bullets: Mei Tanaka reported eleven after-hours pages in two weeks for three platform engineers and about twenty-six estimated hours of unplanned work.
Mei Tanaka said the hiring plan must not be counted as immediate Q4 capacity because a senior hire needs about thirty days to learn the system.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Priya Raman agreed that reliability reserves are planned work and that she would present the three Q4 bets as proposals rather than settled commitments.
Priya Raman and Mei Tanaka agreed to try a forty-five-minute joint scoping session before the next planning cycle’s candidate bets circulate.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Mei Tanaka will send a capacity note by Friday, draft two backend role briefs and an onboarding sketch by next week, and ask an engineer to lead the next optimizer review by end of week.
Priya Raman will schedule the joint scoping session next week and send Mei a revised Q4 draft tomorrow morning.
